episodes.192643: During the late evening hours of July 31st, an MCS brought severe wind gusts to the KC metro. Wind gusts up to 80 mph were reported on the Kansas side of the KC metro, but winds had weakened to 60 to 70 mph through the Missouri side of the KC metro. Widespread power outages were reported. A large percentage of the 60+ mph winds were associated with the gust front/outflow boundary out ahead of the storms.
episodes.192645: During the late evening hours of July 31st, a line of storms brough severe wind gusts to portions of eastern Kansas.
episodes.192689: A remnant southwest to northeast boundary from early morning convection combined with an approaching upper trough and associated cold front, as well as anomalous precipitable water values up to 2.00 inches and CAPE around 2000 J/kg.  Resultant thunderstorms came in two phases, first a marginally severe bow echo that crossed far southwestern central Indiana, and then torrential, training downpours from northern portions of the Indianapolis Metro into Hamilton and Madison Counties.  Impacts ranged from isolated tree damage in both Knox and Daviess Counties, and then rainfall up to 4.50 inches, which included rates up to 3.00 inches/hour, that produced flash flooding in Marion, Hamilton, and Henry Counties.  The greatest impact was significant flooding on Interstate Route 465 on the Fall Creek Bridge that caused long delays during rush hour, while other flooding occurred mainly across eastern Hamilton County.
episodes.192692: Upslope flow and higher moisture across northeast NM behind a backdoor front resulted in an uptick in diurnal afternoon thunderstorm activity August 1st. Storms produced large hail and high wind gusts up to 65 mph and wind damage to Clayton.
episodes.192695: An isolated thunderstorm popped up on the sea breeze in Horry County bringing a brief bout of 1 inch hail.
episodes.192792: Upper level troughing provided another mesoscale convective system to form and propagate through East Tennessee, bringing scattered reports of damaging winds to the area, and localized flash flooding to the northern Plateau.
episodes.192986: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment. A few trees were blown down, and localized flash flooding occurred with slow storm motions.
episodes.193062: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193063: Thunderstorms developed ahead of an upper level disturbance moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.193104: An area of low pressure supported widespread showers and thunderstorms on July 30th and 31st. Slow storm motions allowed heavy rain to fall over the same area, with high rainfall rates over 2 inches per hour.  The most significant flooding occurred over Grafton County where saturated ground conditions and steep terrain supported flash flooding in Piermont.
episodes.193510: A line of strong thunderstorms moved across north central and northeast South Dakota during the morning of July 31st. Wind damage started near Britton, with a tower blown down at the ballpark and several grain bins knocked over. Thunderstorm winds continued east flipping pontoon boats near Lake City. A peak wind gust of 92 mph was measured at the Hillhead Remote Automatic Weather Station around the same time that a roof was partly blow off of a dairy barn near Veblen. That complex of storms continued east into Minnesota during the early afternoon, with additional thunderstorms developing across northeast South Dakota during the afternoon. Those storms produced hail to the size of half-dollars 3 miles north of Sisseton and sporadic tree damage in Codington and Hamlin counties.
episodes.193835: A slow moving low pressure system tracked across Wisconsin during the afternoon hours on Thursday (8/1). Showers and thunderstorms developed in a very moist airmass leading to small hail, gusty winds, and very heavy rain along across portions of central Wisconsin. As much as 3 to 5 inches of rain fell across this region during the afternoon, causing flash flooding and road closures across portions of Marathon, Wood, and Waushara counties.
episodes.193966: A complex of severe thunderstorms moved across the area, producing scattered wind damage across central and north-central Kansas, followed by a more concentrated area of 65-80 mph winds from Topeka to Lawrence.
episodes.194106: A cold front moved southward across Kansas into a hot and humid airmass during the evening hours on the 31st. This sparked off a line of strong to severe thunderstorms which produced damaging to destructive winds across the northern and central Kansas. The Salina area had extensive tree damage and power outages from thunderstorm wind gusts over 80mph with a measurement of 95 mph in downtown.
episodes.194400: Torrential rain rates with hourly rainfall totals up to 2 inches during the evening hours resulted in flash flooding issues developing in the towns of Oakland City and Union in Southwest Indiana. Flooding occurred on side streets and, in Pike County, damaged fencing and carried away items. Precipitable water values were near 2 inches while MLCAPE was 2000 J/kg.
episodes.194573: The passage of weak low pressure and its cold front led to numerous thunderstorms across southern WI. Several funnel clouds were reported. No tornadoes occurred.
episodes.194604: An upper-level low near the northern Baja Peninsula provided strong forcing for ascent across much of the southern half of AZ. This upper-level forcing in combination with MLCAPE values approaching 1000 J/KG, resulted in the development of strong thunderstorm activity across much of southern AZ with additional activity developing in the Yuma area. DCAPE values were in excess of 1500 J/KG and thus conditions were favorable for these thunderstorms to produce strong to severe downburst winds.
episodes.194611: On the evening of July 31st, a cluster of severe storms brought large hail, wind damage and heavy rainfall to portions of southeast Minnesota. In some areas, heavy rainfall totals led to flooding of various roads and low-lying areas in residential communities.
episodes.194668: Storms lined up across central Iowa on the 850 mb moisture gradient early in the morning of July 31, producing up to quarter sized hail and gusts over 50 mph in isolated downbursts. Storms shifted into southeast Iowa through the morning and remained strong, producing hail and strong winds. As storms shifted southeast the orientation shifted to allow for training storms will heavy rain of 3-6 inches in some locations. This area also received heavier rain the previous day when multiple rounds of storms moved across the area, so soils were less able to handle the additional rain. Areas of flash flooding resulting in road closures were reported. After a break in the afternoon and early evening, a bowing line of storms passed across central to southern Iowa. This brough another round of strong winds of 55 to 65 mph and isolated hail up to quarter sized.
episodes.194787: Numerous multicell clusters developed near I-70 and spread east-southeast between about 5 pm and 10 pm, generally across the Ellis, Rush, Trego, Ness, Pawnee, Stafford and Pratt counties.   One inch diameter hail was measured by the public near Trego Center, but the vast majority of the area received heavy rain and there was an overall absence of severe criteria reports.
episodes.194839: An early morning line of showers and thunderstorms intensified during the afternoon upon encountering a favorable environment for severe thunderstorms. Steep mid-level lapse rates combined with strong instability. The storms produced damaging wind gusts which downed trees in several areas and mostly quarter to hen egg size hail, but some hail was much larger.||A hailstone in Stevens County measured six inches in diameter (it was photographed next to a ruler). This at least tied the record for the largest hailstone in Minnesota. Storm Data records also indicate six inch diameter hail in Nobles County on July 28, 1986, and in Murray County on July 4, 1968. The hail was collected about 13 to 15 minutes after the hail ended but was not saved in a freezer.
episodes.194844: A lone supercell thunderstorm tracked from Gregory County South Dakota, into Boyd and far northeastern Holt County during the evening hours of July 31st. Hail up to 2 inches in diameter was reported in far northeastern Holt county. Golf ball sized hail was reported in eastern Boyd county.
episodes.194845: SPC had much of the state, including easter KY in a slight risk for severe thunderstorms for the day Wednesday July 31. According to SPC: Similar to yesterday, a seasonally strong belt of northwesterly flow aloft will persist today from the lower Ohio Valley to the southern Appalachians and coastal Southeast. Much of this will reside atop a moist and very unstable air mass, especially across parts of the lower Ohio Valley to Cumberland Plateau, where upwards of 3000-4000 J/kg MLCAPE may develop by peak heating outside of any MCS-related impacts. This general scenario will likely support several organized severe-producing storms clusters/MCSs through the evening across these regions. Somewhat higher severe probabilities (Enhanced category) may be warranted in subsequent outlooks for parts of these region.||For one, an MCS ongoing across central Illinois this morning may potentially persist southeastward within this increasingly unstable environment, possibly impacting areas such as southern Indiana, southern Ohio and parts of Kentucky/Tennessee with a heightened wind damage potential. Aided by differential heating, scattered storms should also increase across the southern Appalachians vicinity this afternoon, with some organization into clusters possible given the aforementioned relative strength of winds aloft, with wind damage possible.||Sure enough, a line of storms developed around 10am EDT in east-central and KY and moved eastward over the next few hours. By the time it reached Bell County it produced heavy rain that led to flash flooding. The MCS that originated across Illinois continued to push southeast into the region, along with other developing storms. This lead to multiple warnings across the region during the afternoon and early evening hours, and multiple storms that produced damaging thunderstorm winds.
episodes.194919: A couple of thunderstorms developed over Elbert County during the evening and produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195029: A weak surface trough was able to fire up showers and thunderstorms that moved through the area. On storm became severe a produced a severe wind gust over the waters.
episodes.195096: A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present in the wake of earlier day convection, as another stronger mid-level wave and associated frontal boundary pushed through southeast South Dakota and southwest Minnesota during the evening and early overnight hours. Initial development of an isolated supercell in south central South Dakota resulted in hail up to 2 inches in diameter, but more widespread convection along the boundary later in the evening led to areas of damaging wind and excessive rainfall in east central South Dakota and southwest Minnesota. Rainfall was heaviest near the Brookings area with several gauge amounts of 4 to 8 inches around the city.||Indirect fatalities occurred when increasing wave action on an area lake associated with thunderstorm winds resulted in the drowning of two individuals.
episodes.195097: A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present in the wake of earlier day convection, as another stronger mid-level wave and associated frontal boundary pushed through southeast South Dakota and southwest Minnesota during the evening and early overnight hours. Widespread convection along the boundary later in the evening led to areas of damaging wind and excessive rainfall in east central South Dakota and southwest Minnesota.
episodes.195227: A stationary front was located over the lower Ohio Valley from July 30th into July 31st, with upper level flow oriented from northwest to southeast across the region. This upper flow pattern brought multiple waves of showers and thunderstorms across southern Indiana and central Kentucky over this two day stretch. Scattered strong to severe storms mainly produced wind damage, with localized flash flooding also being reported where there was training of multiple rounds of showers and storms.
episodes.195307: A tropical wave crossed the islands during the beginning of August, from Thursday, August 1st, through Saturday, August 3rd, which resulted in an unstable weather pattern. This weather scenario was enhanced by local topography, sea breeze variations, and afternoon effects typically observed in Puerto Rico, resulting in flooding and strong gusty winds due to thunderstorm activity.
episodes.195361: A hot, humid, and very unstable airmass resulted in scattered pulse thunderstorms. Several of these thunderstorms drifted over area waterways resulting in gale- to storm-force wind gusts.
episodes.195374: A thunderstorm produced localized wind damage over a small portion of extreme northwestern Virginia.
episodes.195390: During evening hours, a thunderstorm split and the right-mover produced 1 inch hail for DeKalb County in northwestern MO.
episodes.195410: A robust squall line swept through the I-64 corridor of Southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours on the 1st. Numerous wind damage reports were received, primarily in Wayne, Hamilton, and White Counties with many trees and powerlines damaged along with several farm structures. Utility data indicated that roughly half of Wayne County lost power with this storm line. MLCAPE values were approximately 3000 J/kg, DCAPE around 1000 J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 30 kts. Scattered showers and storms continued through the evening and overnight as a cold front moved through during the night, with storm activity in the later convection remaining sub-severe in Southern Illinois.
episodes.195411: A robust squall line sweeping through the I-64 corridor of Southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours on the 1st crossed into Southwest Indiana, with a weakening trend into mid-afternoon. Only a couple isolated wind damage reports were received in Southwest Indiana, along with minor street flooding in Evansville. MLCAPE values were approximately 3000 J/kg, DCAPE around 1000 J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 30 kts. Scattered showers and storms continued through the evening and overnight as a cold front moved through during the night, with storm activity in the later convection remaining sub-severe in Southwest Indiana.
episodes.195412: A robust squall line sweeping through the I-64 corridor of Southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours on the 1st crossed into Northwestern Kentucky for mid-afternoon. Several trees were damaged in Henderson and Daviess Counties, with the storm line weakening as it moved through the Pennyrile. MLCAPE values were approximately 3000 J/kg, DCAPE around 1000 J/kg, and effective bulk shear was 30 kts. Scattered showers and storms continued through the evening and overnight as a cold front moved through during the night, with storm activity in the later convection generally remaining sub-severe aside from one cell which produced wind damage in McCracken County overnight.
episodes.195675: Through midnight, a cluster of storms brought several severe wind gusts to portions of northern Missouri.
episodes.195676: Through midnight, a cluster of storms brought severe wind gusts to portions of eastern Kansas.
episodes.195728: Ahead of a cold front, a small line of convection, just east of Saint Louis, began to grow into a large bowing segment in the warm unstable environment. As the system traveled through southern Indiana, it produced strong damaging winds, resulting in tree and power line damage.
episodes.195729: Ahead of a cold front, a small line of convection, just east of Saint Louis, began to grow into a large bowing segment in the warm unstable environment. As the system traveled through central Kentucky, it produced strong damaging winds, resulting in tree and power line damage. Some of these falling trees caused property damage in Jefferson County.
episodes.195781: On the morning of Thursday August the 1st, a warm front was draped across portions of the state. The airmass was warm across the state, and storms were already firing off across portions of the state, including eastern Kentucky by 7am. However, the real action would come later in the day. A cold front located across Illinois, still well away from Kentucky, produced a line of storms along it during the morning hours. This line of storms gained strength, becoming a squall line and quickly dropping southeast. It reached central Kentucky by the early evening hours, then eastern Kentucky a couple hours later. By the time it got to eastern Kentucky, the line began to lose it's form, but embedded cells still packed a punch, resulting in numerous warnings across the CWA and just as many reports of wind damage. It began to regain it's linear shape by the time it reached the far eastern portion of the state, finally exiting just between 10 and 11pm EDT.
episodes.195836: Scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in northern Greenville County.
episodes.195841: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.195873: Scattered thunderstorms developed across upstate South Carolina during the late afternoon and evening. One of the storms produced damaging wind gusts in the Greenville-Spartanburg area.
episodes.195874: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina mountains during the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Buncombe County.
episodes.195908: During the afternoon and evening hours on August 1st, a slow moving cluster of thunderstorms brought heavy rainfall across Adams County. This resulted in localized roadway flooding.
episodes.195973: A surface boundary moved south to near Interstate 40 by early afternoon of August 1st.  This boundary moved northward to near the Canadian River Valley by early evening and became a focus for thunderstorms initially near Channing and then near Canadian.  Another cluster of thunderstorms moved eastward from northeast New Mexico and into the western Oklahoma Panhandle and far northwest Texas Panhandle during the early evening.  These two large clusters of storms produced outflow boundaries that collided over the central Texas Panhandle and this collision caused more thunderstorms to develop.  There were several severe wind gusts, mainly in the central Texas Panhandle from Borger to Pampa.  A couple of severe wind gusts occurred outside of thunderstorms in areas of showers where rain was being evaporated under the cloud deck.
episodes.196032: Deep monsoon moisture over easern Arizona allowed at least one thunderstorm with heavy rain to form over the Little Colorado River basin above St Johns.
episodes.196041: An advancing warm front triggered a line of strong thunderstorms during the morning of August 1st.  One cluster of minor wind damage occurred across portions of Sangamon and Logan counties during the pre-dawn hours while another occurred further southeast across Clay and Richland counties toward midday.
episodes.196269: A few thunderstorms with heavy rain occurred early August. The Nixon wildfire also erupted.
